audit.why: Xerath outranges Kassadin at every level: Arcanopulse 750, Eye of Destruction 1000, Shocking Orb 1050, against Null Sphere at 650 and Riftwalk at 500. Pre-6 Kassadin has no way to cross that. Post-6 chained Riftwalks on a 5/3.5/2s cooldown erase it against a champion with no dash.
audit.corrected: EVEN 5.5/10 with a hard early and a decisive late is right for 51.04% over 1254 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 material treated Rite of the Arcane purely as a threat and never mentioned that it is a channel that immobilizes him.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Xerath immobilizes himself and gains numerous long-range barrages', and the kit flags it channel. On a 130/115/100s cooldown, the moment he casts it is the moment he cannot move — which is what makes it a window for you, not only for him.
audit.corrected: mid and spikes[1].text rewritten to state the 5000 range, the 130s cooldown and the self-immobilise.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (a) Six fields name a passive called 'Mage Chief' — Xerath has no such ability. (b) wants.you[0] tells you minions block Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction; neither is stopped by them.
audit.why: Xerath's passive is Mana Surge: autos and kills restore his mana. Arcanopulse 'deals magic damage to all targets hit', i.e. it pierces the wave; Eye of Destruction is called down as an area, not fired through it. Shocking Orb is the one projectile in his kit that a minion eats — and it is his only CC. Separately, Null Sphere 'interrupts channels' and Rite of the Arcane is flagged channel, so your Q cancels his ultimate; and his Shocking Orb / Rite of the Arcane CC cancels your Null Sphere in return, which the missingInteractions entry flags.
audit.corrected: Passive renamed to Mana Surge in whys[1], spikes[0].text, early and wants.foe[1]; the minion-block advice corrected to Shocking Orb only; the channel interaction written into breakdown.cooldowns, mid and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint), and dosFull[2].d called Shocking Orb a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s — 15s is not a rank it has.
The whole matchup is a sequencing problem — his only lockdown is one 13s projectile.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[2].d now say wait-for-what before you do what, with the number attached.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Count it out loud if you must. - Your R Riftwalk has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — 13s at rank 1, 11s at rank 5, and it is the one projectile in his kit a minion eats; step up while it is down. - Rite of the Arcane is a 130s channel at rank 1 and Null Sphere interrupts it outright.

edits.before: Q-shield his key spell, W refund the auto, walk — pre-6 trades are accounting; post-6 add a blink and they're arguments you win.
edits.after: Nether Blade refunds mana every 7s on the empowered auto — his 120-mana Arcanopulse bleeds him faster than farming bleeds you.

edits.before: Xerath burns Shocking Orb (Stun) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Xerath burns Shocking Orb (Stun) on nothing — that is 13s of free ground to walk.

edits.before: Trading like the late game already arrived — a level 5 Kassadin with ambitions is a gold bounty with a shield.
edits.after: Arcanopulse pierces the whole wave and Eye of Destruction falls from above — no minion hides you, only distance does.

edits.before: His stacking Mage Chief passive damage compounds the longer you're forced to farm under pressure.
edits.after: Mana Surge refunds his mana on autos and kills, so the poke never stops for want of a bar.

edits.before: Xerath's Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction poke from safe range shred you before you can even reach melee distance, and Mage Chief passive stacks make every trade one-sided.
edits.after: Arcanopulse pierces the wave at 750 and Eye of Destruction rains down from 1000, both outside anything you own, and Mana Surge keeps refilling the mana that pays for them.

edits.before: Xerath's long-range poke completely outclasses your melee-only kit before level 6 — Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction chip you from a range you can't answer, and Mage Chief passive makes every isolated trade worse for you, so you're forced to farm passively under constant pressure.
edits.after: Xerath's long-range poke completely outclasses your melee-only kit before level 6 — Arcanopulse pierces the wave at 750 and Eye of Destruction lands from 1000, ranges your 650 Q cannot answer, and Mana Surge keeps refunding his bar, so you farm passively under constant pressure.

edits.before: Stack Mage Chief passive for bonus damage on isolated targets
edits.after: Refund mana with Mana Surge to poke without ever stopping

edits.before: Play behind minions to block Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction
edits.after: Stand behind minions — only Shocking Orb is stopped by them

edits.before: His Rite of the Arcane ultimate threatens global poke damage the instant you hit 6, and even with Riftwalk online you lack the HP and burst to punish him from range yet, so the power spike still favors him.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane fires from 5000 range the instant he hits 6, but it is a channel that immobilizes him for its whole duration and Null Sphere interrupts channels, so the barrage that threatens you is also the only moment he cannot move or answer a gank.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane ultimate can snipe you from across the map even through minions, adding global kill pressure right as your Riftwalk unlocks but before you have the HP to tank a rotation.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane fires from 5000 range on a 130s cooldown at rank 1, and it roots him in place while he channels — the level 6 threat is real, and so is the punish window every cast hands you.

notes: 'Mage Chief' is a fabricated ability name and appeared in four writable fields; Xerath's passive is Mana Surge per the kit. All four are corrected here. The minion-block advice in wants.you[0] was also wrong in a way that gets a player killed: Arcanopulse hits all targets in its line and Eye of Destruction is an area drop, so standing behind the wave protects you from neither — only Shocking Orb, his single source of CC, is stopped by a minion.
